text:
A recurring UK complaint about Monzo is **what happens when something goes wrong**: a payment is stopped, an account is frozen, or a scam refund is refused, and the customer struggles to get a clear answer. That’s different from saying most customers dislike Monzo. ([financial-ombudsman.org.uk](https://www.financial-ombudsman.org.uk/decision/DRN-4964429.pdf?utm_source=openai))

- **Frozen accounts and unclear updates.** A security check can be justified, but the wait can still be unreasonable. In one Financial Ombudsman case, a restriction affected a customer’s account for four weeks, and Monzo acknowledged it had taken too long to restore full access. Other customers have complained that their accounts were closed without a clear explanation. ([financial-ombudsman.org.uk](https://www.financial-ombudsman.org.uk/decision/DRN-6033900.pdf))
- **Disputes over scam refunds.** Of the Monzo fraud and scam complaints the Ombudsman resolved in 2025, it sided with the customer in about a third. That’s a real concern, but the figure is for **escalated disputes**, not for everyone who reported fraud to Monzo. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/money/2026/feb/07/monzo-natwest-hsbc-refunds-fraud-scam-fos-ombudsman?utm_source=openai))
- **No branch to walk into.** If you want to discuss a complicated problem face to face, Monzo’s app-first model is a drawback. You can pay cash in at a Post Office or PayPoint, but a fee can apply. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/money/2026/feb/07/monzo-natwest-hsbc-refunds-fraud-scam-fos-ombudsman?utm_source=openai))

For perspective, Monzo **ranked first for overall service quality** among personal current-account providers in Great Britain in the independent Ipsos survey published in August 2026. So I’d read the complaints as useful evidence of *what can go wrong*, not as a picture of the typical customer’s experience. ([ipsos.com](https://www.ipsos.com/en-uk/personal-banking-service-quality-great-britain-august-2026?utm_source=openai))
